{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZY40TA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDAOBk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 71, "title": "Separate stable synthetic identity tokens from pen names in forum headers", "body": "## Problem

Forum reading currently conflates account-style identity with the mutable pen name. At baseline `2b98658aefa20f87e04b51e85ce6748ba4402788`, `src/forums.ts:renderPost` puts the current member handle inside `★タイトル (...)`. `tests/forums.spec.ts` explicitly expects this field to change after a rename. The following title line contains only `post.title`.

The inspected August 1996 records show a parenthesized token distinct from a pen name accompanying the title. This is high-confidence evidence for separating the displayed fields, with moderate confidence in interpreting the token as account-style identity. It does not establish registration rules or automatic nickname handling. [Author-preserved PC-VAN archive](https://someya.sakura.ne.jp/poem/tansi/tansimain.html)

This mismatch predates the EIC change in #70; it is not a regression from that merge.

## Expected outcome

Forum READ output presents a stable, original synthetic identity token in the parenthesized field and the member's pen name separately alongside the title. Renaming a human or resident changes the pen-name display without changing that member's token or post attribution.

Use a documented reconstruction for token assignment, title-line placement and spacing. Preserve the literal authored title and body, including whitespace; add presentation metadata without rewriting stored text. Missing member/name information has a conservative fallback that never exposes internal keys.

## Context

Reproduction: read a locally attributed forum post, change its author's handle, then read it again. Currently the parenthesized identity changes with the handle; expected behavior keeps the synthetic token stable and updates the separate pen name.

Relevant implementation:

- `src/forums.ts` owns the shared renderer for human, seeded and generated posts; `src/navigation.ts:handleForum` supplies members and the shared calendar.
- `Member` currently contains only `id`, `handle` and `actor`; member validation rejects unknown fields. Human rename updates the existing member record. Prefer a small deterministic presentation helper if sufficient. If persistence is necessary, make the minimum compatible change and preserve strict validation and old backups.
- `tests/forums.spec.ts` contains the obsolete rename expectation and existing exact-text/optional-field checks. Repository, resident, composition and production journey tests already cover relevant persistence and interaction behavior.

Historical boundaries: the August 7 and 13, 1996 examples contain alphabetic as well as mixed alphanumeric tokens. Do not mandate a three-letter/five-digit pattern. The archive comes from another SIG and was preserved later with some encoding damage; it cannot authenticate DAISIZEN geometry. It also does not prove whether pen names were manually included in titles, automatically inserted, or refreshed after renaming. Showing the current handle separately is an accepted product reconstruction, not an authenticated historical rename rule. [Preserved records](https://someya.sakura.ne.jp/poem/tansi/tansimain.html)

An undated participant reference describes registered nicknames affecting mail display; that evidence is specific to mail and does not resolve forum policy. [Participant reference](https://www2s.biglobe.ne.jp/nozomin/kanri/pcvan.html)

This refines [#41](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/41), which deliberately replaced technical IDs with friendly presentation, while restoring the synthetic-ID distinction anticipated by [#7](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/7). Preserve #41's unobtrusive presentation and inspectable provenance. Live open-Issue and open-PR searches returned no items; bounded history inspection found no equivalent pending handoff.

[PR #70](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/70) and `docs/validation.md` report 254 passing checks for the baseline. Those are Coordinator records; this research graph did not rerun them.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Render separate synthetic identity and pen-name fields for human, seeded and generated forum posts. Tokens remain stable across handle changes, repeated reads, reloads and JSON export/restore, independent of member-array order. Different members sharing a handle remain distinguishable.
- [ ] Use original, recognizably synthetic tokens. Never print raw UUIDs, `fictional-ai:*` keys, record-key substrings, real archived identities or provenance metadata as account tokens. Do not introduce authentication or change the scripted connection identity.
- [ ] Define safe behavior for old imports, missing members, blank/unusable handles and existing `DEMO` fixtures. Unknown attribution must not become a fabricated authenticated account. Browsing must not seed or rewrite imported content merely to obtain display tokens.
- [ ] Preserve post/member IDs, author references, titles, bodies, timestamps, calendar projection, reply relationships, numbering and read markers. Keep mail addressing, mail/OLT/conference presentation, resident scheduling, consent and reset/import semantics outside this correction. Any necessary supporting storage change remains backward compatible and atomically validated.
- [ ] Replace the obsolete handle-in-parentheses assertions and add focused coverage using the existing Playwright setup. Cover human and resident renames, duplicate handles, member ordering, seeded and mocked generated posts, legacy/missing authors, reload and backup/restore stability, and unchanged source records. Verify exact Japanese title/body whitespace and literal markup rendering.
- [ ] Include a production-browser READ → HANDLE rename → READ → reload/restore journey. Verify separate fields, stable identity and preserved authorship. Retain existing composition, storage, consent, IME and terminal regression coverage; no real inference or model download is needed.
- [ ] Update `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md`, its synthetic header example and relevant About/README descriptions. Record source URLs, access date, target-year scope, confidence, token-assignment assumptions and unresolved nickname behavior. Keep research explanations in existing provenance surfaces.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test`, whose configured servers include TypeScript checking and the production build, and records actual results. Review the final diff, affected documentation links and `git diff --check`. Use existing tooling without introducing another framework.

## Optional validation

An additional visual comparison of the synthetic header with the cited archive may help assess readability. Exact historical spacing, human confirmation and hardware checks are not completion gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks can be completed before merge.
